payload.content: The key difference is Read View lifetime. Under RC, each consistent read gets a fresh Read View; under RR, the first consistent read generally establishes one reused by later consistent reads. Why does that difference affect whether a later commit becomes visible?

Because RC recalculates the visibility boundary for the next read, so a transaction that committed in between can become visible. RR reuses the earlier snapshot boundary, so the later commit can remain invisible to snapshot reads.
Good. New scenario: T1 under RR does a snapshot read. T2 updates the row and commits. T1 does another snapshot read, then a locking current read. What distinction matters?

The second snapshot read stays on T1’s existing Read View and can return the old version through the undo chain. A current/locking read is not the same snapshot mechanism and reads the latest qualifying version while taking locks, so it can observe a newer committed value subject to locking.
Summarize RC versus RR in one sentence without using the phrase “repeatable read means repeatable”.
RC refreshes the consistent-read snapshot per statement; RR normally reuses the transaction’s established consistent-read snapshot, so later commits do not automatically enter that snapshot.
